question: Should OpenClaw enforce safe embedded-SQLite patch floors immediately, or stage the compatibility break through a warning period?
rationale: The upstream safety requirement is clear, but enforcement intentionally invalidates currently supported and installer-provided runtimes and therefore needs explicit maintainer ownership.

options.title: Enforce safe floors now
options.body: Raise the supported Node floors, remove the obsolete odd-numbered line, add startup and doctor diagnostics, and ship coordinated upgrade guidance in one compatibility change.

options.title: Warn then enforce
options.body: Add diagnostics and release warnings first, then make affected embedded SQLite versions fatal after a defined upgrade window.

options.title: Document residual risk
options.body: Keep the current runtime contract and document the rare corruption exposure without enforcement.

recommendation.title: Enforce safe floors now
recommendation.body: Raise the supported Node floors, remove the obsolete odd-numbered line, add startup and doctor diagnostics, and ship coordinated upgrade guidance in one compatibility change.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the adjacent SQLite lifecycle work, authored this compatibility proposal, and are the current assignee.
